ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Theoretical Framework for Randomized Shapley Value Estimators
PROPOSAL: Develop a unified theoretical framework that captures the essential components of randomized Shapley value estimators, including KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP. This framework will provide a platform for analyzing the trade-offs between different design choices, such as sampling distributions, weighting schemes, and constraint sets.
CONTROLS: Derive a common expression for the Shapley values as the solution to a constrained least-squares problem, and then analyze the effect of different randomized estimators on this problem.
COST: 7200 
PREDICTION: We propose that this framework will provide valuable insights into the relationships between different randomized estimators and help identify the key factors that contribute to their success or failure in practice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Implementation of LeverageSHAP using Approximate Nearest Neighbors
PROPOSAL: Develop an efficient implementation of LeverageSHAP using Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN) techniques. This implementation will utilize ANN algorithms, such as HNSW or Annoy, to speed up the calculation of leverage scores and sampling of rows in the regression problem.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of our ANN-based implementation with the standard implementation of LeverageSHAP, and evaluate the effect of different ANN parameters on the performance.
COST: 10800 
PREDICTION: We expect that our ANN-based implementation will provide significant speedups compared to the standard implementation of LeverageSHAP, especially for large datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring the Use of Gradient Boosting Machines for Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of Gradient Boosting Machines (GBMs) for Shapley value estimation. Specifically, design a GBM-based estimator that utilizes gradient boosting to learn the Shapley values directly from the data.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of our GBM-based estimator with existing Shapley value estimators, including KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP.
COST: 16200 
PREDICTION: We expect that our GBM-based estimator will provide competitive performance with existing Shapley value estimators, especially for complex datasets with non-linear relationships.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Effect of Feature Engineering on Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of feature engineering on Shapley value estimation. Specifically, explore how different feature engineering techniques, such as correlation analysis, mutual information, and dimensionality reduction, impact the quality of Shapley value estimates.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of Shapley value estimators on datasets with manually engineered features versus datasets with automatically engineered features using different techniques.
COST: 24300 
PREDICTION: We expect that feature engineering will have a significant impact on the quality of Shapley value estimates, with carefully engineered features improving the accuracy of estimates and poorly engineered features degrading their accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Large-Scale Benchmarking of Shapley Value Estimators
PROPOSAL: Develop a large-scale benchmarking framework for Shapley value estimators, including KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, SimSHAP, and the hybrid approach proposed in this work. The framework will include a variety of datasets and evaluation metrics to comprehensively assess the performance of different estimators.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of different estimators on a range of datasets, including tabular datasets, image datasets, and text datasets.
COST: 36000 
PREDICTION: We expect that the benchmarking framework will provide valuable insights into the strengths and weaknesses of different Shapley value estimators, and help identify areas for future research and improvement.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Long-Range Temporal Dynamics in MLLMs for Change Understanding
PROPOSAL: We will modify a multimodal large language model (e.g., CLIP-ViT) to integrate temporal information from satellite image time series data and train it to capture long-range temporal dynamics. The model will learn to predict the next image in the sequence by conditioning on the entire historical context, and it will also be able to describe the changes that occurred over time.
CONTROLS: We will compare our model to state-of-the-art image captioning models (e.g., SceneGraph) and temporal forecasting approaches (e.g., Temporal Fusion Transformers).
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Our modified MLLM should outperform baselines in both image captioning and future forecasting tasks, especially when the sequence has a long temporal span, but its performance might suffer when the model needs to describe complex, fine-grained changes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Future Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will design a suite of metrics and quantitative evaluation approaches to assess the temporal consistency of predicted future images, including metrics that measure the likelihood of observed trends, the similarity of predicted changes to historical patterns, and the coherence of predictions with respect to the underlying semantic drivers of change.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate our metrics on satellite image time series data (e.g., Alos-2, QuickBird, WorldView-2) and compare the performance of different forecasting models (e.g., Temporal Fusion Transformers, Graph-Based Forecasting) when using these metrics.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: The proposed metrics should provide a comprehensive evaluation framework for temporal consistency in future satellite image forecasting, and models optimized for these metrics should significantly outperform state-of-the-art approaches in terms of temporal consistency, but may not necessarily achieve better image quality or other evaluation metrics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enhancing Long-Range Temporal Understanding for Joint Change Description and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will develop a two-stage pipeline that first employs the modified MLLM from proposal 1 to generate a rich semantic description of past changes, and then uses this description as input to guide a future forecasting model (e.g., a variant of Temporal Fusion Transformers) to generate the predicted future image.
CONTROLS: We will compare our two-stage pipeline to models that directly predict future images from satellite image time series data (e.g., state-of-the-art future forecasting models) and to models that generate change descriptions and forecast future images separately.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The two-stage pipeline should significantly outperform state-of-the-art approaches in terms of both change description accuracy and temporal consistency of future forecasting, but it may introduce additional computational cost due to the two-stage process.

TITLE: Quantifying the Impact of Long-Range Temporal Dynamics on Forecasting Performance
PROPOSAL: We will design a series of experiments to quantify the impact of long-range temporal dynamics on the performance of future forecasting models, including analyses of the effect of different temporal sampling rates, the impact of long-range dependencies on forecasting accuracy, and the role of long-range temporal dynamics in capturing complex change patterns.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of forecasting models that capture long-range temporal dynamics to models that do not, and evaluate the effect of different temporal sampling rates on model performance.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Our analysis should provide insights into the importance of long-range temporal dynamics for accurate forecasting, and help to identify key challenges and opportunities for future research.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Testing for Temporal Consistency in Future Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will develop an adversarial testing framework to evaluate the robustness of future forecasting models to/elicit(er) fine-grained temporal inconsistency, and use it to identify vulnerabilities in current models and pinpoint areas for improvement.
CONTROLS: We will test our framework on state-of-the-art future forecasting models (e.g., Temporal Fusion Transformers) and analyze the types of adversarial attacks that are most effective in exploiting temporal inconsistency.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: Our framework should help to improve the robustness and reliability of future forecasting models, but may require significant computational resources due to the complexity of adversarial testing.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Enhancing Long-Range Temporal Understanding for Joint Change Description and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will extend the two-stage pipeline from proposal 3 by incorporating the long-range temporal dynamics captured by the modified MLLM in proposal 1, and evaluate the impact of this integration on the performance of the pipeline in both change description and forecasting tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare the integrated pipeline to the original two-stage pipeline and to separate models that only capture long-range temporal dynamics or only perform change description and forecasting.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: The integrated pipeline should achieve better performance in both change description and forecasting tasks, especially when the sequence has a long temporal span, but may introduce additional computational cost due to the increased complexity of the model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Dataset for Evaluating Change Description and Forecasting in Satellite Image Time Series
PROPOSAL: We will collect and curate a large-scale dataset of satellite image time series, with corresponding change descriptions and forecasted images, to provide a standardized benchmark for evaluating the performance of models in both change description and forecasting tasks.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the performance of state-of-the-art models on our dataset and compare their performance to models that are specifically trained on the dataset.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: Our dataset should provide a valuable resource for the research community and help to drive progress in both change description and forecasting tasks, but may require significant resources for data collection and curation.

ACTION: REVISE 6
TITLE: A Dataset for Evaluating Change Description and Forecasting in Satellite Image Time Series
PROPOSAL: We will include additional annotations and labels in our dataset, such as class labels for change types, severity levels, and spatial distribution, to enable more fine-grained evaluation of model performance in change description and forecasting tasks.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the impact of additional annotations on model performance and compare the performance of models trained on the annotated dataset to those trained on the original dataset.
COST: 6800
PREDICTION: The additional annotations should improve the discriminatory power of our dataset and enable more accurate evaluation of model performance, but may require significant additional resources for annotation and data curation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Adapter Positioning in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of several commonly used adapter positions (before the last layer, after the last layer, after the input layer, after the output layer) within a given online time series forecasting framework, such as OGD, on real-world datasets like M4, Caspian, and even traffic flow data from the INRT dataset.
CONTROLS: baselines include frozen model, updating last layer only, and several off-the-shelf online time series forecasting algorithms like GRAD-Fu and StreamFOREGround.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: I expect the adapter before the last layer to achieve state-of-the-art results on most datasets, as it gives the least opportunity for error and noise to accumulate before correction, and fine-tuning the last layer is often crucial for fit; adaptation in early layers might fail due to vanishing gradients.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bypassing Gradients with Linear Adapters: An Empirical Study
PROPOSAL: Investigate the online time series forecasting performance of directly fitting the parameters of a linear adapter on a small batch of recent samples, using datasets like M4 and Caspian in traffic flow, and on real-world traffic flow data.
CONTROLS: ablation study on the adapter size, learning rate and schedule to establish when and why linear adapters outperform or fall behind favoured gradient-based methods.
COST: 530
PREDICTION: I expect the linear adapter model to obtain competitive results on short-term forecasting tasks but struggle with longer-term predictions and larger datasets, due to overfitting, and perform worse when there's considerable concept drift in the data.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Adapter Positioning in Online Time Series Forecasting with an Emphasis on Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Modify proposal 1 to include a comparison of the performance of adapter positions when given delayed and noisy feedback in multi-step forecasting tasks, using real-world datasets M4, Caspian, and a traffic forecasting dataset, and develop a multi-step extension for the identified best adapter position.
CONTROLS: after comparing performance consider multi-step variants of each adapter position studied in the original proposal, with lag introduced by simulating later steps of forecasting; and we benchmark results against off-the-shelf methods designed specifically for multi-step forecasting.
COST: 680
PREDICTION: I expect adapter positions that can account for delayed updates with a reasonable lag (e.g. <5 time steps) perform relatively better, and current selection to have significant impact with specified implementations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adapter-Gradient Trade-offs in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Investigate how varying amounts and combinations of adapter weights and gradient descent influence forecasting performance on different datasets and tasks, including experiments on varying adapter sizes and learning rates, and considering both short-term and multi-step forecasting tasks, using datasets like M4 and traffic flow data.
CONTROLS: control experiments include single-parameter sweeps on the learning rate and adapter size and studying combinations (low learning rate and large adapter, low learning rate and small adapter, high learning rate and small and large adapters) in pairs with baseline methods.
COST: 740
PREDICTION: Large amounts of adaptation with strong gradient updates should generally lead to better initial performance, but as time goes on or concept drifts emerge, models with less adaptation may remain competitive and even show improvements; and better performance on the short-term predictions having decreased impact on overall effectiveness.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: A Comprehensive Exploration of Adapters for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Combine and revise proposal 1, 2, and 3 by comparing the forecasting performance of models with different types of adapters (linear, model-based, ensemble-based), varying sizes and complexities, and applied at different positions within the model architecture, using datasets like M4, Caspian and real-world traffic data, and assessing both short-term and multi-step forecasting.
CONTROLS: thorough ablation studies of adapter sizes, learning rates, and complexity are performed to get socket parameterizations finding optimal performance parameters for each model-type and each position.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: With such a comprehensive analysis, the previously-identified adapter-type and position optimals should hold not just on best-case datasets but also more generally, except in few edge cases with very high noise or drift rates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Time-Series Dependent Adapter Selection for Pre-Trained Forecasters
PROPOSAL: Develop a system that automatically selects the adapter type, size, and position based on the characteristics of the time series being forecasted, such as seasonality, trend, and noise levels, and evaluates its performance on datasets with varying patterns, including those from traffic flow, electricity consumption, and weather forecasting.
CONTROLS: controls will include adapter selection based on static features, static features combined with adapter performance, as well as state-of-the-art online time series forecasting algorithms like ETS and Prophet.
COST: 1738.4
PREDICTION: The proposed adapter selection system should result in significant performance improvements over pre-set adapter configurations, and ensure better-than-naive performance in conditions of distribution shifts; and further investigation into how the time series automatically selected might fail.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Efficient Experience Replay with Attention Mechanisms for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Modify proposal 2 by incorporating attention mechanisms into the experience replay system, enabling it to selectively replay the most relevant past samples when adapting to changing conditions, and evaluate its impact on forecasting performance, using datasets from various domains, including traffic flow and weather forecasting.
CONTROLS: compare the performance of attention-based and baseline experience replay systems, including the case without any replay mechanism, under scenarios with different levels of concept drift and sample sizes.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: By focusing on the most relevant past samples, attention-based experience replay is expected to significantly improve adaptation efficiency and maintain or further enhance forecasting performance under drift conditions; failure may occur with drawn-out, gradually-changing processes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Lag Implementation for Robust Multi-Step Forecasting in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Introduce an adaptive lag mechanism that dynamically adjusts the forecasting horizon based on the model's performance and the characteristics of the time series being forecasted, and evaluate its impact on forecasting performance, using real-world datasets from various domains, including traffic flow and weather forecasting.
CONTROLS: compare the proposed adaptive lag approach against fixed lag implementations, including scenarios with varying lag sizes, and assess the effect of adaptive lag on forecasting performance under different levels of concept drift and sample sizes.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: I expect the adaptive lag implementation to improve forecasting performance and robustness by allowing the model to dynamically adjust to changing conditions, achieving results that are superior or comparable to fixed lag implementations under most scenarios, except potentially during catastrophic shifts.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Unified Framework for Online Time Series Forecasting with Adapters, Lag, and Experience Replay
PROPOSAL: Combine and integrate the various components explored in the previous proposals (adapters, lag, experience replay) into a comprehensive unified framework for online time series forecasting, and conduct a thorough evaluation of the framework's performance on diverse datasets, including real-world examples from traffic flow, weather forecasting, and more.
CONTROLS: experiment with various configurations and hyperparameter settings to identify the most effective combination of components, and perform extensive ablation studies to understand the individual contributions of each component.
COST: 4600
PREDICTION: I expect the unified framework to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across the evaluated domains, and show that the integrated approach can provide improved robustness and adaptability compared to configurations that utilize individual components in isolation, with potential exceptions under particularly challenging drift conditions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Online Time Series Forecasting with Adapters and Lag
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework for analyzing online time series forecasting with adapters and lag, including a study of the dynamic regret of the unified framework proposed in proposal 6, and provide a theoretical justification for the empirical findings obtained in the previous proposals, applying tools from online learning and convex optimization.
CONTROLS: consider the efficient ridge estimator and empirical risk minimization as the underlying risk minimization guarantees; provide regret bounds using similar arguments to those in bandit theory.
COST: 5800
PREDICTION: I expect the theoretical analysis to provide insights into the properties of online time series forecasting with adapters and lag, including convergence rates and optimality guarantees, and demonstrate that the combined approach offers improved theoretical guarantees over individual components, with some caveats regarding the convergence rate of adaptive lag under specific modeling assumptions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lightweight Dense Text Retriever for Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: 
We propose "DocLite", a lightweight dense text retriever designed to complement strong vision-centric multimodal encoders for visual document retrieval. DocLite will be a simplified version of the Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) model, trained on a subset of the PubMed corpus and fine-tuned on a small synthetic dataset of abstracts and their corresponding document images. DocLite's output will be a single vector of 128 dimensions, allowing for efficient similarity computation with the vision-centric retriever.

CONTROLS: We will compare DocLite with a strong baseline of the BM25 sparse lexical representation on the PubMed and Core17 datasets, and measure its performance with and without the vision-centric retriever.

COST: 5040
PREDICTION: With the correct hyperparameter tuning, DocLite will achieve close to state-of-the-art results on visual document retrieval benchmarks, particularly when combined with the vision-centric retriever. The main challenge lies in finding the right trade-off between model capacity and efficiency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Aggregated Similarity Scores for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: 
We propose to modify the DocLite retriever to produce multiple vectors, each representing a different aspect of the text (e.g., title, abstract, body). We will then aggregate the similarity scores between the text and image representations using these multiple vectors. This can be done using a simple average, weighted average, or even a neural network-based approach.

CONTROLS: We will compare the aggregated similarity scores with the single-vector output of DocLite, and evaluate both on the PubMed and Core17 datasets. We will also compare our method with the standard hybrid retrieval approach, where the text and image retrievers produce separate similarity scores that are simply added together.

COST: 7200
PREDICTION: Our aggregated similarity scores approach will outperform both the single-vector DocLite and the standard hybrid retrieval approach on the visual document retrieval benchmarks. However, the best aggregation method may depend on the specific datasets and models used.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: REVISED: Aggregated Similarity Scores for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: 
We revise our previous proposal to instead use a neural network tofuse the similarity scores from the text and image retrievers, rather than simply aggregating them. This network, which we'll call the "Hybrid Fusion Network" (HFN), will take the similarity scores from the text retriever and the image retriever as input, and produce a single similarity score that combines the information from both.

CONTROLS: We will compare the HFN with both the single-vector DocLite and the standard hybrid retrieval approach, and evaluate all on the PubMed and Core17 datasets. We will also examine the effect of varying the size and complexity of the HFN on the performance of the hybrid retrieval system.

COST: 10800 
PREDICTION: Our HFN will outperform both the single-vector DocLite and the standard hybrid retrieval approach on the visual document retrieval benchmarks, and will do so with a smaller increase in the size and complexity of the model. However, the optimal architecture of the HFN may depend on the specific datasets and models used.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Indexing for Hybrid Retrieval Systems
PROPOSAL: 
We propose to investigate efficient indexing strategies for hybrid retrieval systems, where the text and image retrievers produce separate similarity scores that are combined using the HFN. One potential approach is to use an inverted index that combines the word frequencies from the text retriever with the visual features from the image retriever. Another approach is to use a separate index for each retriever, and then use a re-ranking stage to combine the results.

CONTROLS: We will evaluate the proposed indexing strategies on the PubMed and Core17 datasets, and compare their performance to a baseline approach that uses a single, unified index. We will also measure the memory and computation requirements of each indexing strategy.

COST: 5040
PREDICTION: The proposed indexing strategies will significantly reduce the memory and computation requirements of the hybrid retrieval system, while maintaining or improving its performance on the visual document retrieval benchmarks. However, the optimal indexing strategy may depend on the specific datasets and models used.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Batch Processing for Hybrid Retrieval Systems
PROPOSAL: 
We propose to investigate batch processing approaches for hybrid retrieval systems, where multiple queries are processed simultaneously. One potential approach is to use mini-batch processing, where small batches of queries are processed together, and the results are then combined. Another approach is to use block processing, where large blocks of queries are processed together.

CONTROLS: We will evaluate the proposed batch processing approaches on the PubMed and Core17 datasets, and compare their performance to a baseline approach that processes queries one at a time. We will also measure the memory and computation requirements of each batch processing approach.

COST: 7200
PREDICTION: The proposed batch processing approaches will significantly reduce the computation time of the hybrid retrieval system, while maintaining or improving its performance on the visual document retrieval benchmarks. However, the optimal batch size and processing approach may depend on the specific datasets and models used.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning to Combine Text and Image Retrieval Models
PROPOSAL: 
We propose to train a neural network to learn how to combine the outputs of text and image retrieval models to produce the final retrieval results. The network will take the output of the text retriever and the image retriever as input, and produce a single output that combines the information from both. The network will be trained using a reinforcement learning approach, where the rewards are based on the relevance of the retrieved documents.

CONTROLS: We will compare the proposed approach with the baseline approach of simply combining the output of the text and image retrievers using a weighted average. We will also evaluate the approach on a variety of visual document retrieval tasks and datasets.

COST: 8640
PREDICTION: The proposed approach will significantly outperform the baseline approach on visual document retrieval tasks, particularly when the text and image retrievers have different strengths and weaknesses. However, the optimal architecture and training objectives for the learning-to-combine network may require careful tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Modal Interactive Retrieval
PROPOSAL: 
We propose to extend the learning-to-combine network to an interactive retrieval system, where the user can provide feedback on the retrieved documents, which is then used to update the ranking of the documents. The system will use a multi-modal architecture, combining text, image, and user feedback modalities to produce the final retrieval results.
